# Moons

> Moons is a full-stack TypeScript framework (file routing, SSR, React hydration)
> whose single guarantee is zero-trust: `*.server.ts` modules become typed RPC
> stubs, and leaking server code fails the build.

Site: https://docs.devmoon.net
Agent context bundled with the CLI: `node_modules/@moonsjs/cli/docs/ai/CONTEXT.md`
(also used by `moons-mcp` `search_docs`).

## Get Started
- [Installation](https://docs.devmoon.net/getting-started/installation): Create a Moons app with the CLI, understand what the scaffold contains, and verify it with a green check run.
- [Your First App](https://docs.devmoon.net/getting-started/first-app): Add a route, link pages together, load data on the server, and call your first server function.

## Core Concepts
- [Zero-Trust Model](https://docs.devmoon.net/core-concepts/zero-trust): What the zero-trust guarantee covers, what stays public, and what remains your responsibility.
- [Routing](https://docs.devmoon.net/core-concepts/routing): File conventions, dynamic params, nested layouts, navigation signals, and error boundaries.
- [serverFn](https://docs.devmoon.net/core-concepts/server-fn): Declare server-only functions with typed schemas, call them from loaders or the browser, and revalidate with refresh().
- [Loaders](https://docs.devmoon.net/core-concepts/loaders): How loader exports run, the LoaderArgs contract, layout loader data, devalue serialization, and the public-data rule.
- [Context & Environment](https://docs.devmoon.net/core-concepts/context-and-environment): Create per-request context in moons.config.ts, type it with typegen, and keep secrets in env() while public values use VITE_*.
- [Navigation & Search Params](https://docs.devmoon.net/core-concepts/navigation): Client-side navigation with Link, prefetching, pending UI, search-param parity with loaders, and refresh() after mutations.
- [Error Handling](https://docs.devmoon.net/core-concepts/error-handling): Custom 404 and error boundaries, redirect and notFound signals, and the [moons] error format with its machine-readable catalog.

## Guides
- [Authentication](https://docs.devmoon.net/guides/authentication): A session pattern built on context, signed cookies, loader and serverFn guards, and rate limiting.
- [Working with Databases](https://docs.devmoon.net/guides/databases): Keep database clients on the server, query them through server functions, and run migrations with plain Bun scripts.
- [API Routes](https://docs.devmoon.net/guides/api-routes): Raw HTTP endpoints under src/api, from file mapping and method handlers to an explicit security model.
- [Middleware](https://docs.devmoon.net/guides/middleware): Directory middleware in the routes and API trees, global middleware in config, and the exact request order.
- [Forms & Mutations](https://docs.devmoon.net/guides/forms): Submit an HTML form to a server function, validate with one schema, show pending and error states, and refresh loader data.
- [Deployment](https://docs.devmoon.net/guides/deployment): Build output, running the production server, static hosting, edge behavior from config, and Docker.
- [Behind Cloudflare](https://docs.devmoon.net/guides/behind-cloudflare): Run the Moons server behind the Cloudflare proxy: trusted client IPs, origin lockdown, caching, rate limits, and Turnstile.
- [Prerender & ISR](https://docs.devmoon.net/guides/prerender-and-isr): Build-time rendering with prerender and paths, incremental revalidation, shared ISR storage, and when to use each mode.
- [Testing](https://docs.devmoon.net/guides/testing): Test routes, schemas, and API handlers with moons test, then smoke-test the production build.
- [Migrating from Next.js](https://docs.devmoon.net/guides/migrating-from-nextjs): Map App Router and Pages Router concepts to Moons, port a small posts app step by step, and see what the framework deliberately leaves out.
- [Migrating from Remix + React Router v7](https://docs.devmoon.net/guides/migrating-from-remix): Move Remix and React Router v7 loaders, actions, and route modules to Moons, port a notes app, and see what the framework deliberately leaves out.

## API Reference
- [@moonsjs/core](https://docs.devmoon.net/api/core): The config helper and validated config keys, the error model, routing signals, and request-scoped response helpers.
- [@moonsjs/server](https://docs.devmoon.net/api/server): serverFn, environment access, signed cookies, rate limiting, validation, and request-scoped helpers for server code.
- [@moonsjs/react](https://docs.devmoon.net/api/react): Link and navigate, the data and navigation hooks, routing signals, and the client hydration entry for React route files.
- [@moonsjs/vite](https://docs.devmoon.net/api/vite): The Vite plugin that scans routes, generates types, enforces the server/client boundary, and verifies the client bundle.
- [CLI](https://docs.devmoon.net/api/cli): The moons command line for scaffolding, the dev/build/start loop, verification with check and test, and JSON introspection with routes, fns, errors, and audit.
- [@moonsjs/mcp](https://docs.devmoon.net/api/mcp): A stdio MCP server that exposes routing, verification, audit, scaffolding, and documentation tools to MCP clients.

## Recipes
- [Notes App](https://docs.devmoon.net/recipes/notes-app): Build a small notes app with a shared schema, a server-only store, a loader, and a mutation that refreshes the list.
- [Protected Route](https://docs.devmoon.net/recipes/protected-route): Read a signed session cookie in context, guard a page loader, and issue or clear the session with server functions.
- [Form Submission + Revalidation](https://docs.devmoon.net/recipes/forms-revalidation): Validate a form on both sides, submit it to a server function, refresh the loader, and keep a no-JavaScript fallback working.

## Architecture
- [Architecture](https://docs.devmoon.net/architecture): Why the server/client boundary is dangerous, the three layers that enforce it, and the limits you still own.

## Packages

`@moonsjs/core` · `@moonsjs/server` · `@moonsjs/react` · `@moonsjs/vite` ·
`@moonsjs/cli` · `@moonsjs/mcp` — developed in the open at github.com/moonsjs.
